stemMd: A manufacturer attributes the longer life of its new batteries to a redesigned casing. Which experiment would best test that attribution?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Compare batteries with and without the new casing while holding their internal components and operating conditions constant.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Ask buyers which battery packaging they prefer.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Measure only batteries that lasted unusually long.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Compare the new batteries with much older batteries stored in a different climate.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Compare the prices of several brands.

explanationMd: Change the proposed cause while controlling other relevant differences. A casing comparison with identical internals and operating conditions isolates the feature under investigation far better than comparisons involving age, climate, or brand.

distractorRationale.b: Preference does not measure battery life.
distractorRationale.e: Price comparisons do not isolate casing effects.
distractorRationale.c: Selecting on the outcome would bias the test.
distractorRationale.d: Age and climate would confound the casing comparison.
